What It Does for a Round Face: A fringe swept from a deep part lays a diagonal across the forehead so the eye travels sideways-down instead of around the cheek curve - the close nape keeps the lower silhouette narrow
Length Band: Fringe sweeps past the cheekbone; nape tapered close but not shaved
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Bangs cut to fall past the eyebrow; point-cut ends keep the fringe moving instead of lying as one block
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Ear-length sideburn pieces in front of the ears cover the widest point of the cheekbones; shape trims every 4-5 weeks to keep the nape defined

What It Does for a Round Face: One side cut visibly longer than the other disrupts the left-right symmetry a round face presents as width
Length Band: Longer side drops toward the cheekbone or jaw; opposite side cropped close to the ear
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: At least an inch of difference between the two sides (about 2.5 cm); the longer side needs enough density to hold its shape without looking stringy
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: The longer side doubles as the fringe; shorter side tapered or slightly undercut around the temple - on curly hair the longer side can spring wide so diffuse it

What It Does for a Round Face: Shattered piecey top work breaks the smooth cap of hair that would mirror the face's roundness; the vertical piecework stacks the eyeline upward
Length Band: Crown left about 3-4 inches (7.6-10.2 cm); sides kept close
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Thinning shears and point cutting all over the top - but not overlayered because the top needs some weight to fall into shape
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Fringe broken into uneven pieces rather than one horizontal line; tapered sideburns; trims every four weeks

Pixie Style: Long Pixie / Bixie with Curtain Fringe
What It Does for a Round Face: Extra top and front length gives the frame a vertical line to travel while the curtain split draws two diagonals down past the temples
Length Band: Front sits between the cheekbones and the jawline; bixie length at or just above the jaw
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Light layering through the crown for brushable height; feathered crown layers cut long and swept back
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Curtain fringe parts at the centre and sweeps outward along the cheekbones; face-framing tendrils optional; trims every five weeks

What It Does for a Round Face: Clipped-away sides delete the volume at the temples; the height the top keeps reads taller against the bare sides
Length Band: Sides at clipper length or shaved; top left substantial enough to style upward
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Disconnected - the top drops off sharply into the sides instead of blending gradually
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: No fringe needed; sideburn area clipped with the sides. The undercut runs its own clock: one guide schedules its trims every three weeks another every 4-6 weeks - set the real interval with your stylist

What It Does for a Round Face: Curls kept long on top build the height while tapered sides stop the curl mass from ballooning at the cheeks
Length Band: Extra length on top and through the front so the curls form volume upward not outward
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Interior layering removes weight from underneath while preserving curl definition on top; cut it dry - shaped wet coils can pouf out at the sides
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: Sides and nape lightly tapered or undercut so the curl silhouette stays narrow; styling by diffuser not brush-out

What It Does for a Round Face: A very short fringe plants a horizontal accent high on the forehead - and the guides split on whether that helps or hurts a round face: some style it as angle-up-high flattery while others file blunt micro bangs under avoid. Both positions are stated in the row; settle it with your stylist
Length Band: Micro fringe sits just above the brows
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Keep the fringe edge feathered with soft point cutting - a hard blunt edge is exactly what the avoid-list guides object to
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: The fringe is the feature; sides stay close and tapered; fringe trims every three weeks

What It Does for a Round Face: The whole top styled upward into one vertical mass - the most literal height a round face can wear with flat sides sharpening the contrast
Length Band: Crown long enough to grab and lift; sides flat against the head
Layering & Where the Cut Starts: Quiff built by blow-drying the top forward and upward then set with pomade and hairspray
Fringe & Sideburn Pairing: No fringe - the lifted front is the front; trims every four weeks hold the proportions
